#9080. Thai Massage Therapy: Benefits and What to Expect

Feeling stressed? Whether you unwind with yoga or a relaxing massage, Thai massage combines the best of both worlds, benefiting your mind and body. Here’s everything you need to know!

Thai massage is a special kind of bodywork that blends relaxation with flexibility. Think of it as a gentle, full-body, more active experience. It’s all about boosting your flexibility and energizing your body. Just a heads-up: napping during a Thai massage might be a challenge!

Drawing from Ayurvedic and traditional Chinese medicine, this ancient technique mixes assisted yoga stretches, acupressure, and soothing rocking for 60 to 90 minutes. Unlike Western-style massages at a local spa, Thai massage takes place on a mat on the floor. A certified therapist will work to stretch your muscles and apply pressure along your body’s energy lines, known as sen, to release stress with a graceful, rhythmic touch.

You can schedule a Thai massage at many spas, massage clinics, and even some yoga studios, but make sure you find someone with the proper training and certification to give you an authentic experience.

When you arrive for a Thai massage, you might be given some comfy clothes, like a T-shirt and drawstring pants. You’ll remove your shoes, silence your phone, place your jewelry in a small dish, and settle onto a floor mat. Before the session, let the therapist know if you have any injuries.

If this is your first session, it can be intense, so focus on breathing and relaxing. You’ll likely start on your back, with the therapist beginning on your feet and legs. Since the therapist uses their body weight to guide you, it might initially feel a bit weird. Some discomfort is normal as your body stretches, but don’t hesitate to let your therapist know if anything feels uncomfortable.As the session progresses, you’ll likely switch positions, including flipping onto your belly or trying various other postures. Go with the flow as your therapist guides you through stretches and yoga-like moves designed to open up your joints, move your energy, and release tension. Keep breathing and communicate with your therapist throughout the process.

As the session wraps up, you’ll enjoy some gentle rocking motions to ease you out of the massage. You might feel sore afterward, especially if it’s your first Thai massage, so hydrate and rest. You’ll likely feel incredibly relaxed, more flexible, and energized.

Pro tip: Clear your mind and be open to guidance. While the stretches may feel awkward initially, allow yourself to let go. This can help you fully experience the massage’s benefits.

Your Thai massage experience won’t resemble a Western-style deep tissue massage. You won’t be naked under a sheet on a raised massage table, and the massage therapist won’t be using long, deep strokes to work your muscles.The other significant difference is that, like some forms of yoga, Thai massage has a spiritual element based on Buddhism. As they use the weight of their bodies to work on your body, your therapist is also trained to send you kind, loving, healing vibes. The ultimate goal is to help you feel better by allowing your energy to flow throughout your body.

The ancient practice of Thai massage combines assisted yoga stretches, acupressure, and rhythmic rocking to unknot your body and get your inner energy flowing. Unlike Western massage techniques, you’ll be fully clothed on a floor mat, with the massage therapist using their entire body to release your tension.

Permit yourself to let go, and expect an active, sometimes intense, full-body experience that leaves you relaxed and energized.

Last medically reviewed on July 31, 2024

#9079. Synthesis of the Arts: The Case for Beauty in Architecture and the City

This article is part of "Thresholds", a special edition printed newspaper by Cobe Notes x ArchDaily.

This article is part of "Thresholds", a special edition printed newspaper by Cobe Notes x ArchDaily.

Post–World War I modernism broke sharply with historicist and neoclassical traditions, stripping buildings of ornamentation and historical or religious reference to focus on priorities, clarity, and efficiency. Architecture embraced rationality and social reform, while art moved in the opposite direction, exploring self-expression, experimentation, and freedom from academic conventions.

Architecture embraced rationality and social reform, while art moved in the opposite direction, exploring self-expression, experimentation, and freedom from academic conventions.

This tension between objective order and subjective perception has defined a threshold between the arts evident in contemporary architectural practices, where personal intuition increasingly gives way to measurable facts. Is our pursuit of answers, facts, and truths distancing us from something fundamentally human: questions, doubt, and ambiguity? The answer may lie in public, building-integrated art, a practice that sits precisely at that threshold, and asks practitioners in architecture and urban design to trust values that resist direct measurement.

AC Milan and FC Internazionale Milano (Inter) have unveiled the design for Generali Stadium, a 71,500-seat venue planned to become the shared home of the two football clubs in Milan, Italy. Designed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, the new stadium will be built alongside the existing San Siro as part of a 281,000-square-meter redevelopment of the surrounding area. The project follows years of discussions over the future of the historic venue, which the clubs acquired in 2025 with the intention of replacing it. Construction is expected to begin in 2028, with the stadium scheduled to host its first match during the 2031/32 season, subject to planning approvals.

Diamond-shaped entrances lead into panoramic concourses, while a double-curved roof establishes the building's overall profile. Measuring approximately 244 by 270 meters, the roof incorporates a spoke-wheel structural system and 27,500 square meters of photovoltaic panels. The design also includes naturally ventilated spaces, rainwater harvesting, greywater recycling, and high-efficiency LED lighting. The stadium is planned as an all-electric facility, with the project targeting LEED Gold certification and carbon-neutral operation.

The proposal marks the latest development in a process that began in 2019, when the two clubs first announced plans to replace San Siro. Opened in 1926 as AC Milan's home ground, the stadium became a shared venue in 1947, when Inter moved in. Also known as Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, it has undergone several expansions and renovations, most notably ahead of the 1990 FIFA World Cup, and has hosted domestic and international football matches, as well as major concerts. Previous redevelopment discussions included proposals to renovate the existing structure, while a new stadium scheme by Populous was selected by the clubs in 2021. These plans did not proceed, and the debate over the venue's future continued amid discussions concerning its architectural significance and heritage protection.

The proposal marks the latest development in a process that began in 2019, when the two clubs first announced plans to replace San Siro. Opened in 1926 as AC Milan's home ground, the stadium became a shared venue in 1947, when Inter moved in. Also known as Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, it has undergone several expansions and renovations, most notably ahead of the 1990 FIFA World Cup, and has hosted domestic and international football matches, as well as major concerts. Previous redevelopment discussions included proposals to renovate the existing structure, while a new stadium scheme by Populous was selected by the clubs in 2021. These plans did not proceed, and the debate over the venue's future continued amid discussions concerning its architectural significance and heritage protection.

In September 2025, the Milan City Council approved the sale of the stadium and surrounding land to the two clubs, which subsequently acquired the property for €197 million. The new development is intended to extend beyond the stadium itself, introducing public spaces, landscaped areas, retail, and leisure facilities designed to remain active throughout the year. The clubs estimate the new stadium's construction cost at approximately €1.2 billion and have also secured a naming-rights agreement with Italian insurance company Generali, reportedly valued at €650 million through 2052. However, the decision to replace San Siro continues to face opposition from some supporters and heritage advocates. During the design unveiling on October 29, 2026, a group of Inter fans protested against the plans, displaying a banner calling for the preservation of the existing stadium. San Siro is expected to remain in operation until the new venue opens, after which most of its structure is planned for demolition.

#9075. Tiered immigration hub by Aedas opens at Shenzhen-Hong Kong border

Photography courtesy of Aedas (unless stated otherwise)

Architecture studio Aedas has completed a tiered, round-edged building designed to accommodate an immigration hub between Hong Kong and Shenzhen, China.

Perched on the banks of the Shenzhen River, the New Huanggang Port Development opened earlier this month in replacement of the original Huanggang Port, which first opened between the two cities in 1989.

Conceived by Aedas as a “large-scale integrated hub”, the nine-storey facility combines border control and transport networks with 25,000 square metres of public space.

Its stacked volume is complete with a “flowing facade” formed of horizontal metal fins, while its rounded form was designed to evoke a pebble, in reference to its riverside location.

“The grounded, rounded form responds to the building’s large scale and waterfront setting, evoking a pebble resting on the banks of the Shenzhen River,” the studio told Dezeen.

“Flowing metal fins wrap the elevation like ribbons, reinforcing the building’s fluid appearance and symbolising the close connection between Shenzhen and Hong Kong.”

“[The building’s] integrated transport networks, flowing facade and welcoming civic spaces express the close relationship between the two cities while establishing a distinctive point of arrival,” the studio added.

A modular, prefabrication approach was employed to construct the building’s volume, which opens up at ground level via two sunken plazas and is topped with a solar panel-covered roof terrace.

Across its four elevations, its rhythmic horizontal fins have been lifted to form large glass curtain walls that draw daylight into the interior.

Inside, the hub’s transport, immigration and public programmes are stacked vertically and connected by a network of internal escalators.

To accommodate an expected average of 200,000 passengers per day, two of these floors have been dedicated to immigration halls complete with a “barrier-free” design.

Direct connections to transport networks are provided on the floors below, where the hub links to four of Shenzhen’s rail and metro lines to “support a seamless border-crossing journey”.

“Transport, immigration and public programmes are vertically organised under one roof,” the studio said.

“The nine-storey building uses vertical stacking to organise pedestrian crossing, vehicle crossing, public transport and civic amenities efficiently within a constrained site, separating passenger and vehicular flows while maintaining convenient connections between programmes,” it added.

A series of structural, arched columns informed by Shenzhen’s emblem flower – the Bougainvillea – divide the expansive interiors, which are illuminated by 73 roof skylights, facade openings and an integrated lighting system.

Nearby, RHSP has unveiled designs for a skyscraper with a “striking butterfly layout” and MAD has completed a series of boulder-like galleries across a green-roofed museum.

Photography courtesy of Aedas (unless stated otherwise)

The cost of a will varies dramatically based on how you create it and how complex your estate is. Here is a comprehensive comparison of every method, from free options to premium attorney packages.

Several factors push will costs toward the higher end of each range:

The will vs trust decision is primarily a financial calculation: does the upfront cost of a trust save more than it costs by avoiding probate?

When you die with only a will (no trust), your estate must go through probate — a court-supervised process where a judge validates your will, your executor inventories assets, debts are paid, and remaining assets are distributed. Probate costs include:

Probate also takes 6-18 months on average and is a public proceeding — anyone can look up your will, your assets, and who inherited what.

A revocable living trust costs $1,500-$5,000 upfront but avoids probate entirely. The math is straightforward:

For most FI-focused households who are building wealth toward financial independence, the trust pays for itself many times over. If your net worth exceeds $100,000-$200,000 and you own real estate, a trust is almost certainly the better financial decision.

Even with a trust, you still need a pour-over will — a short document that catches any assets not transferred into the trust during your lifetime and directs them into the trust at death. You also still need a healthcare directive and durable power of attorney. Most estate plan packages include all four documents together.

The sticker price of a will is only part of the total cost of estate planning. Several hidden costs catch people off guard:

The FI-optimized approach to estate planning minimizes cost without sacrificing protection:

Start with an online will now. A $159 Trust & Will plan gives you a will, healthcare directive, and power of attorney today. Do not let perfect be the enemy of done — having a basic will is infinitely better than having no will while you save up for an attorney.

Upgrade to a trust when your net worth exceeds $200,000. At this point, the probate avoidance savings justify the $1,500-$3,500 cost of adding a trust.

Shop attorney fees aggressively. Estate planning is a competitive market. Get quotes from at least three attorneys. Many offer flat-fee packages, and prices can vary by 50-100% for the same work in the same city. Ask specifically whether the quote includes trust funding assistance and deed transfers.

Use online services for updates. Rather than paying an attorney $200-$500 for a codicil, many online platforms let you update your will for free or for a small annual subscription ($19-$39/year). Trust & Will, for example, includes one year of free updates.

Bundle documents. An estate plan package (will + trust + POA + healthcare directive) typically costs 20-40% less than purchasing each document separately. If you are going to see an attorney, get everything done in one engagement.

Here is the counterintuitive truth: the most expensive estate plan is the one you never create. Dying without a will (intestate) triggers state default rules that may not match your wishes, longer and more expensive probate proceedings, and potential family conflict. For parents of minor children, it means a judge — not you — decides who raises your kids. The $0-$259 cost of an online will is trivially small compared to these consequences.

Yes. FreeWill (freewill.com) offers a free basic will funded by nonprofit partners. Some states also accept handwritten (holographic) wills that cost nothing. Military personnel can get free wills through the JAG office on any military installation. Many bar associations and legal aid societies offer free will clinics several times per year. While these free options work for simple estates, you may want to pay $99-$259 for a more comprehensive online service that includes healthcare directives and power of attorney.

Attorneys charge $300-$750 for a simple will and $750-$1,500 for a complex will with special provisions. A complete estate plan package (will, trust, power of attorney, healthcare directive) runs $1,500-$5,000. Fees vary significantly by location — attorneys in major metros charge 2-3 times more than attorneys in smaller cities for the same work. Always ask for a flat fee rather than hourly billing for estate planning.

For straightforward estates, yes. Major online will makers like Trust & Will, Nolo WillMaker, and LegalZoom produce documents that are legally valid in all 50 states and cover the same core elements an attorney would include. The difference is that an attorney can provide customized advice, handle complex situations, and anticipate issues specific to your state law. If your estate is simple, an online will is functionally equivalent. If your situation has any complexity, the attorney consultation is worth the additional cost.

Online services typically include free updates for one year and then charge $19-$39 per year for ongoing access. An attorney charges $100-$500 for a codicil (formal amendment) or $300-$1,000 to draft a new will. For minor changes, a codicil is sufficient. For major changes (new spouse, additional children, significant asset changes), creating an entirely new will is cleaner and reduces the risk of conflicting instructions.

The most expensive part of estate planning is NOT the documents — it is probate. Probate costs 3-7% of your estate value ($15,000-$72,000 on a $500,000-$1,000,000 estate) and takes 6-18 months. By comparison, even the most expensive estate plan package ($5,000-$10,000) is a fraction of what your family would spend navigating probate without a trust. The second most expensive mistake is outdated beneficiary designations on retirement accounts, which can send six or seven figures to the wrong person with no legal recourse.

The cost of a will ranges from $0 to $10,000+ depending on your method and complexity, but the most expensive option is always having no will at all. For most FI-focused households, start with an online will for $0-$259 to get basic protection in place immediately. As your net worth grows beyond $200,000, invest $1,500-$5,000 in a comprehensive estate plan with a revocable living trust — the probate savings alone deliver a 300-1,000% return. Update your beneficiary designations today (free), review your plan every 3-5 years, and remember: the goal of estate planning is not to create perfect documents. It is to protect the people you love from financial chaos during the worst moment of their lives.

#9073. Nopales Benefits: Why You Might Add Cactus to Your Diet

Looking at a cactus with its threatening spikes and tough skin, you might not immediately think, “Yep, that’s a thing I could eat.” But guess what? Some forms of cacti are edible, tasty, and quite good for you!

Check out why it might be a good idea to pal around with nopales, the pads of the prickly pear cactus.

The nopal cactus, also known as the prickly pear or the opuntia, is a shrub-like, flowering cactus native to parts of Mexico, Arizona, the Mediterranean, Australia, and other desert regions. It might be recognized by its multitude of connected pads with flowering blooms. (A pad in bloom looks a little like a flat, green paw.)

Nopales flowers are filled with a viscous, seeded substance often used in jams, jellies, pies, cakes, and other sweets. But the stems, leaves, and entire pad (with spines removed, obvs) are also edible. Traditional Mexican preparations include boiling, grilling, and sautéing.

Science is still examining the possible benefits of nopales, so some touted wellness perks are fairly tentative. Here’s a look at what we know about these desert fruits.

Almost any time you see bright colors in edible fruits, it’s a sign they contain antioxidants. This is def true for Nopales!

Older studies have found that the fruit inside their flowers is rich in antioxidants like ascorbic acid, phenolics, and a mixture of betacyanin and betaxanthin. These compounds help fight inflammation by kicking harmful free radicals out of your cells.

Since they combat inflammation, the antioxidants in prickly pear could improve joint mobility. In a 2020 study, people who drank 3 ounces of prickly pear juice daily for 8 weeks had better range of motion and greater ease with daily activities than a control group who drank a placebo.

Research suggests nopales may help steady blood sugar. A 2014 study found that people with type 2 diabetes who ate nopales with a high-carb breakfast had significantly lower blood sugar and insulin levels compared to those who didn’t. However, this study only included 14 participants.

In 2019, a larger systematic review assessed the fruit’s potential for blood sugar regulation. While it found insufficient evidence to support using nopales to reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes, the authors noted it might significantly reduce blood glucose levels.

Showing your liver some love might involve adding nopales (or a glass of nopal juice) to your diet. According to research from 2023, this has to do with prickly pear’s effects on triglycerides. By helping reduce triglyceride accumulation, nopales could relieve stress on the liver.

Whether you’ve overdone it on booze or are down with a stomach bug, it’s important to rehydrate with a drink that contains electrolytes. Consider prickly pear juice as your back-on-the-wagon beverage. It’s got potassium, magnesium, and calcium to help rebalance your electrolyte levels.

If you can track down fresh nopales where you live, cooking it yourself is a fun (if somewhat complicated) way to take advantage of its benefits. If not, look for prickly pear products, such as juices, being sure to check for added sugars.

You can also take a supplement. Nopales supplements typically contain 500-650 milligrams (mg) per day.

While a prickly pear smoothie or nopales salad can be a healthy addition to your diet, consuming this cactus fruit may have some less-than-desirable side effects, like:

If you’re new to nopales, take it slow at first to see how your body responds.

Don’t let the “prickly” in prickly pear keep you away from this desert gem. When prepared correctly, nopales are unique, nutritious food. Check ’em out when your fruit basket needs something a little different.

#9072. Lacaton & Vassal wins Le Prix Charlotte Perriand 2027

The Créateurs Design Association & Awards has named Pritzker Prize-winning French studio Lacaton & Vassal Architectes the recipient of the Le Prix Charlotte Perriand 2027.

Lacaton & Vassal Architectes, which is led by architects Anne Lacaton and Jean-Philippe Vassal and known for its social housing designs, was recognised for contributing to contemporary architecture by transforming and improving existing buildings.

The Créateurs Design Associates (CDA) said the studio’s work improves “living conditions while preserving resources and architectural heritage”.

The duo said it was “very happy” to receive the award.

“Charlotte Perriand’s tireless pursuit of comfort, well-being, and the pleasure of the inhabitant and of everyday life, her modernity, and her political commitment to exposing poor housing conditions and to transmission and education remain profoundly relevant today and are a source of inspiration,” Anne Lacaton and Jean-Philippe Vassal said.

“Her manifest spirit of openness and freedom touches us deeply. We are very happy to receive this distinction.”

The architects founded their studio in 1989 and have since worked on high-profile projects such as the transformation of the Palais de Tokyo in Paris, the Nantes School of Architecture and the Cité du Grand Parc housing transformation in Bordeaux.

The latter, which was completed with Frédéric Druot and Christophe Hutin, won the European Union’s Mies van der Rohe Award in 2019.

Lacaton & Vassal Architectes’ other social housing projects include the renovation of the 1960s Tour Bois-le-Prêtre tower block in Paris, also in collaboration with Frédéric Druot, which was completed in 2011.

It also converted and extended a former shipbuilding workshop to create the FRAC Nord-Pas de Calais contemporary art gallery in Dunkirk.

The Le Prix Charlotte Perriand was established in collaboration with the family of the late architect and recognises practitioners whose contributions have advanced architecture and design.

“In awarding Le Prix Charlotte Perriand to Lacaton & Vassal, the CDA members recognise the care and imagination with which they approach the places people call home. Their work shows how much can be gained by understanding what is already there,” Créateurs Design Association co-founder Meredith Xavier said.

The award will be given to Lacaton & Vassal Architectes in a ceremony on 16 January 2027, at the Shangri-La Paris. Architect Kengo Kuma will also be honoured at the event as the winner of the Andrée Putman Lifetime Achievement Award 2027.

Lacaton & Vassal Architectes has previously won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2021, as well as the 2023 Soane Medal for architecture.

Last year, Lacaton won the 2025 Jane Drew Prize for women in architecture.

#9071. Lion Green Road / Mary Duggan Architects

Text description provided by the architects. Lion Green Road is a residential-led scheme comprising five buildings containing 157 dwellings. #9070. Herzog & de Meuron and EHDD to Transform a Mid-Century Warehouse for the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity

The Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity has unveiled the masterplan for its forthcoming archives in Marin County, California. The project, designed by Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron and Bay Area-based EHDD, transforms a mid-century modern warehouse into a cultural destination, with art installation space, flexible galleries, learning and gathering spaces, a theater, and dining offerings. The large-scale adaptive reuse project is accompanied by a transformation of the gardens and grounds of the surrounding 88.5-acre site, led by Field Operations. While the Institute's Eames Archives will form one part of the museum, its exhibitions and programming are intended to extend far beyond the work of Charles and Ray Eames, bringing together different disciplines, creative processes, and ideas.

The large-scale adaptive reuse project is accompanied by a transformation of the gardens and grounds of the surrounding 88.5-acre site, led by Field Operations. While the Institute's Eames Archives will form one part of the museum, its exhibitions and programming are intended to extend far beyond the work of Charles and Ray Eames, bringing together different disciplines, creative processes, and ideas.

In August 2025, the Eames Institute acquired the roadside campus in Novato, California, on the 60th anniversary of its completion. The industrial building, known for its folded, origami-like white hyperbolic paraboloid concrete roof, was designed in the 1960s by Polish-born American architect Jan Lubicz-Nycz for the office of modernist architect John Savage Bolles. It was commissioned by the McGraw-Hill publishing company as a textbook publishing, warehouse, and distribution facility. The company left the facility in 1991, and the building later served as headquarters and warehouse for Birkenstock USA. Today, the project to transform the complex into a new multidisciplinary museum by 2030 is in the first phase of the review, permitting, and approval process with the City of Novato.

With an emphasis on showing process and ideas, the Institute is collecting works ranging from industrial design and painting to monumental works of art and public sculpture, to be housed in the converted warehouse. Herzog & de Meuron's project preserves the hyperbolic paraboloid roof while integrating new building systems. The former industrial building will open to the landscape with new recessed glass facades and porches along its north and south sides. The new spaces respond to the geometry of the existing structure, with a material palette of color-stained plywood, plaster, and aluminum windows that complements the preserved concrete structure. Visitors are expected to arrive through a new exterior room carved into an existing landscape berm, the Arrival Court, where the building can be seen against an infinity-edge fountain in the foreground.

The 185,000-square-foot interior is organized as a series of interconnected experiences, starting with a wood-clad space housing admissions, the museum shop, lockers, restrooms, and elevators. A grand staircase connects to a 120-foot polished stainless steel bridge that appears to float across the warehouse, offering views into the central Great Hall and the exhibitions below. The Great Hall will be 400 feet long by 120 feet wide and will host art installations and galas. Six interconnected galleries; making and collection spaces, including wood and ceramics workshops; storage, library and resting rooms; and a 275-seat theater for performing arts, film screenings, speaker series and live concerts form the rest of the cultural spaces. The complex also includes a café, a bistro, and a fine-dining restaurant with views over the surrounding landscape.

As an extension of the museum experience, Field Operations is redesigning the exterior of the complex, drawing on Marin County's oak savannas, coastal prairies, woodlands and meadows. The firm has selected native and climate-adapted plantings to create varied landscapes connected by a network of trails. According to the architects, the landscape project builds on the original approach of landscape architect Tito Patri, whose design used layered berms to integrate the buildings into their surroundings and buffer the campus from the highway, with new and existing berms framing public gardens and gathering spaces. Field Operations also cites as a reference the Eameses' Powers of Ten, a nine-minute short documentary written and directed by the couple, which explores the relative scale of the universe.

New exterior features include native stormwater gardens and wet meadows throughout the campus to capture and filter rainwater; interactive landscape features and custom furnishings designed by Field Operations; children's play spaces drawing on the firm's work on the Bay Area's Tunnel Tops Park; a tree-filled upper court that turns a former employee parking area into a gathering space next to the museum's café, bistro and restaurant; a redesigned parking and arrival area; and large gardens to the north and south of the warehouse in place of former truck turnarounds and loading docks. An adjacent 45,000-square-foot former office building will be restored as a pavilion for retreats, lectures, seminars, and other gatherings, with meeting spaces and a large multipurpose room overlooking the warehouse roof. Behind the pavilion, a Japanese-inspired garden will incorporate historic concrete relief murals by artist Gurdon Woods, carved into the existing retaining walls.

The Institute extends the designers' approach across Northern California, adding to the material legacy of Case Study House No. 8, commonly known as the Eames House. #9069. Ultimate Guide to 4A Hair: Care Tips, Styles, and Maintenance

Understanding your hair type is key to achieving healthy, luscious curls. Hair types range from 1 to 4 — straight, wavy, curly, and coily — with type 4 being the curliest. Type 4A hair has a fine texture and loose curl pattern, forming springy coils that need special care to stay healthy and vibrant.

Knowing your hair type helps determine the best hair care routine. Caring for 4A hair is essential, whether you’re dealing with dryness or breakage or want to define your curls.

Let’s dive into the world of 4A hair and discover how to keep those curls popping.

Alright, curl friends, let’s break it down. Hair type falls into four main categories:

Now, Type 4 hair is where things get seriously curly and coily. Within this category, we’ve got subtypes A, B, and C,

which refer to the width and density of your curls.

So, what’s the deal with 4A hair? 4A hair is the queen of the fine, loose curl pattern. It forms tight, springy coils that are like tiny, perfect S-shapes. These curls are less dense than their 4B and 4C cousins, making them more defined and delicate. Think of 4A hair as the Goldilocks of coily hair — not too tight, not too loose, but just right.

Your hair is unique and gorgeous, but it requires a bit of extra TLC to keep it looking its best. Here’s a straightforward guide to keeping your 4A hair moisturized, healthy, and thriving:

4A hair tends to be dry as its coily structure makes it difficult for natural oils to travel down the hair shaft. Keeping it moisturized is essential, so incorporate a good leave-in conditioner into your daily shampooing routine. Use deep conditioning treatments weekly to replenish moisture and strengthen your curls.

Don’t forget scalp care, too! For maximum hydration, look for products with ingredients like shea butter, coconut oil, and glycerin.

4A hair is prone to tangles, so detangle gently to avoid breakage. Use a wide-tooth comb or your fingers to work through knots carefully. Start from the ends and work your way up to the roots, and always detangle when your hair is wet and coated with conditioner to provide slip and minimize damage.

Heat styling tools can cause significant damage to 4A hair, leading to dryness, breakage, and loss of curl pattern. Minimize the use of blow dryers, flat irons, and curling wands. If you use heat, always apply a heat protectant spray first to shield your hair from high temperatures.

Pro tip: To maintain the health of your curls, opt for air-drying or styles that don’t require heat.

Protective styles like braids, twists, and buns can help reduce manipulation and minimize breakage. These styles tuck away your ends, protecting them from friction and environmental damage.

Cotton pillowcases cause friction, which leads to frizz and breakage, especially for 4A hair. Switching to satin or silk pillowcases instead helps mai

ntain your curl pattern and prevent tangles.

Regular trims are crucial for keeping 4A hair healthy and preventing split ends from traveling up the hair shaft. Aim to trim your hair every 8-12 weeks to remove damaged ends and keep your curls looking fresh and vibrant.

Yes, 4A hair is curly and falls under the coily category. It features tight, springy curls that form an S-shape.

To determine your hair type, look at the curl pattern, texture, and density. 4A hair has a loose curl pattern with fine, springy coils, while 4B and 4C hair have tighter curls. 3C hair is curly but not as tight as Type 4.

Washing once a week or every two weeks is generally sufficient for 4A hair. Overwashing can strip the hair of its natural oils.

Regular trims every 8-12 weeks help keep 4A hair healthy by removing split ends and preventing breakage.

Taking care of your 4A hair isn’t rocket science, but it does need a little know-how and the right tools.

Love those natural curls — keep them hydrated, avoid excessive heat, and give them some nighttime TLC.

#9068. Eight architecture and design events in November from Dezeen Events Guide

Miami art week, Design Doha Biennial, Dubai Design Week and the Dezeen Awards 2026 party are among the key architecture, design and art events featured in Dezeen Events Guide this November.

Other events taking place during the month include Collectible New York, Cairo Design Week, Irish Design Week and BDNY.

Dubai Design Week celebrates its 12th edition in 2026, returning with a programme of fairs, exhibitions, installations, talks and markets.

The festival’s headline event Downtown Design takes place from 4 to 8 November in the city’s design district and welcomes brands such as Trika Arabia, Bottega Living, Biscuit, Alain Ellouz Paris and 1971 – Design Space.

Other events in the lineup include the competition-winning Urban Commissions installation by Dubai-based NAO Architects and the In Other Words group exhibition.

5 November 2026 to 31 Janaury 2027, Qatar

The second edition of the Design Doha Biennial celebrates design, architecture and craft from the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia (MENASA) region.

The festival programme features exhibitions, talks, installations, awards and other pop-up events, including the latest edition of Arab Design Now, which showcases projects from 81 participants.

Taking place at 210 East 86th Street, annual design fair Collectible New York presents works and talks from global designers and galleries.

Spotlighting contemporary pieces, the fair is separated into four categories: the Main exhibition, Fashion, Bespoke and New Garde.

The event follows Collectible’s Brussels edition, which took place earlier this year in March.

2026 marks the fifth edition of Irish Design Week, which takes place at multiple venues across Ireland, including the Royal Irish Academy of Music.

The festival celebrates regional design, architecture and craft through exhibitions, summits, open studios, workshops, awards and talks.

Returning to the Javits Center in New York City, the exhibition and talks series at this year’s Boutique Design New York (BDNY) follows the theme Designed to Be Remembered.

The showcase highlights furniture, textiles and lighting, focusing on “unforgettable” materials and small details, with more than 700 brands taking part in the fair.

This year’s Dezeen Awards party takes place in London‘s Royal Opera House, where the winners of 49 project categories will be announced, as well as the architecture, interiors and design projects of the year, six Designers of the Year and the Regional Showcases.

The event celebrates the work of the designers and architects with refreshments and music. The dress code is dress to impress!

There are three districts participating in the 2026 edition of Cairo Design Week: Heliopolis, Zamalek and Downtown.

The design week spotlights Egyptian creativity, from its contemporary design to the capital‘s historic architecture.

The festival programme includes exhibitions, installations, tours of often-private properties and talks.

Dezeen Events Guide will launch its annual guide to Miami art week, accompanied by an interactive map to help you navigate the city.

The week-long festival takes place across Miami, with fairs, exhibitions, talks, pop-ups, open showrooms, tours and parties spanning Miami Beach and Miami Design District.

Two of the largest events include the Design Miami and Art Basel Miami Beach fairs, running from 1 to 6 December and 4 to 6 December, respectively.

#9066. 5 Signs You’re in a One-Sided Friendship, According to Experts

Welcome to Asking for a Friend, a weekly series dedicated to solving the messy, awkward, and confusing parts of modern friendship. Because truth is, our platonic relationships are often the most complicated. Send us your friendship dilemmas here, and we might feature one in a future column.

Most friendships will never be truly 50/50, but at the very least they run on an unspoken agreement: both people show up, reach out, and add some fuel to the tank that keeps the engine going. If that balance consistently feels off—not just once or twice, but over the course of weeks or months—it’s hard not to wonder whether something deeper is going on.

You might notice in small but telling ways: Looking back at your messages, it dawns on you that you’re initiating every conversation. They call, if at all, only when they’re bored or when it’s convenient. And then there’s the sharper sting of noticing how effortlessly they find time for other people—just not for you (a surprisingly common frustration you can read more about here).

To be fair, life can get in the way—people get busy, schedules clash, and our friends can’t always be as available as we’d like—but that doesn’t make it any less frustrating or stop you from feeling resentful when you’re waiting days for a simple “How are you?” But how do you know if this is a temporary lapse or a more unhealthy one-sided friendship? Here are the biggest red flags therapists want you to watch out for.

Look through your texts and DMs: Are you always the first to send a message? When’s the last time they suggested hanging out? You can also experiment by not reaching out to see how long it takes for them to initiate contact. If weeks (or months) go by without a word, their silence may indicate who’s really holding this connection together.

“At a minimum, a good friend (even a busy one) will periodically check in out of curiosity and interest,” Tiana Leeds, LMFT, a therapist based in Santa Barbara, California, tells SELF. After all, someone who truly cares about you should want to know what’s going on in your life, which is why if they consistently don’t try to get in touch (or only expect you to do so), they may not be genuinely interested in your world.

Venting to your friends is natural—some would even argue it can strengthen your bond. That said, being there for each other is supposed to be a two-way street, Hope Kelaher, LCSW, author of Here to Make Friends: How to Make Friends as an Adult, tells SELF.

If someone unloads their laundry list of problems but doesn’t listen to yours, “they’re likely using you as their on-call therapist,” Kelaher says. This one-directional dynamic could look like a person who constantly complains about their boss but changes the subject whenever you open up about your work-related stress. Or they dominate dinner conversations with their dating disasters, yet they’re “busy,” uninterested, or MIA when you need relationship advice. Over time, investing all your time and energy into people who won’t give back can drain your energy, Leeds says, and leave you feeling neglected by a person who’s supposed to have your back.

Maybe they insist on eating at restaurants near their place, which means you have to travel across town every single time. They only reach out when “better” plans fall through (“Hey, my dinner got canceled. What are you doing tonight?”), making you feel more like an afterthought than a priority. More subtly, perhaps they’re only interested in brief 15-minute coffee chats that fit their schedule instead of a dedicated dinner or movie night.

“In a healthy relationship there should always be a give-and-take,” Kelaher says, meaning both people need to compromise. So it’s disheartening when, again and again, someone you’d do anything for won’t meet you halfway (sometimes literally).

Your friend might be a workaholic or chronically forgetful (which, don’t get us wrong, is still frustrating). But that alone doesn’t mean your bond is one-sided.

Instead, “consider the bigger picture and ask yourself, ‘Is their behavior a reflection of not caring about me, or just a difference in availability and communication style?’” Leeds says. As an example, someone who takes five business days to reply to anyone’s messages may not be singling you out. What’s more telling, though, is if that same person who’s “too swamped” to text you regularly posts Instagram stories of brunches, dinners, and post-work meetups with others in their social circle. Or if your usually punctual friend (who’s known for being reliable) is comfortable canceling plans only with you. These inconsistencies, Kelaher says, suggest that they’re perfectly capable of showing up—just not for you.

Let’s say you mentioned how important it would be to have support at your first 5K race. A friend who truly cares might surprise you at the finish line with flowers, or at the very least shoot over a heartfelt “Good luck!” or “Congrats!” In a one-sided friendship, however, this kind of consideration may be missing entirely. They might downplay your achievement (“Sorry I couldn’t make it, but it was such a short race!”) or forget your big day without a hint of apology.

True friends go the extra mile to celebrate your successes and be there during tough moments. That’s why if someone repeatedly forgets significant events like your birthday, or rarely shows empathy for your challenges (like a scary medical procedure, a high-stakes presentation), they may not be as invested as they should be.

Therapists recommended bringing up your concerns non-confrontationally.

Ideally, their response can give you a glimpse into whether they’re aware of this imbalance and, more importantly, if they’re willing to work on it. That said, you can’t force someone to be a good friend, so if they don’t care enough to show up for you, know that you deserve better. “After all, friendships take work, Leeds says. “But it’s not meant to be done by just one person.”

#9065. Pucker Up! How to Heal Cracked Lip Corners Fast

Smiling for selfies should be fun, not painful! If cracked lip corners or angular cheilitis make it hard to smile, eat, or kiss, don’t worry. Check out these tips to heal those cracks quickly. With some care and good habits, you’ll have pain-free, makeout-ready lips in no time. Say goodbye to angular cheilitis and hello to a happier smile!

The first step to healing your cracked lip corners quickly is to lock in any moisture. Reach for a product dermatologists call an occlusive, which creates a protective barrier that prevents your lip corners from getting drier. Vaseline, Aquafor, or CeraVe ointment are common occlusives that will help reduce cracking.

Dab a little coconut oil, olive oil, or fragrance-free moisturizer on the corners of your lips daily after you shower. Make it a daily habit, but don’t go overboard. A little dab will do. Allow your skin’s natural oils to build back up as the cracking fades. Bonus tip: Add the occlusive lip barrier after moisturizing.

Locking in moisture only works if you have enough moisture, so staying hydrated is key! Keep a refillable water bottle with you as your trusty sidekick. Sip on plain water throughout the day, or jazz it up with a splash of cucumber or another non-acidic flavor. Pro tip: Avoid lemon juice, which can irritate and sting sensitive skin.

Bonus: Staying hydrated will help your raw lip corners heal quicker and improve your skin’s overall health.

Have you noticed that moisture is a common theme here? Lend your lips a humid hand by sleeping with a humidifier beside your bed. Adding moisture to the air is especially helpful for your cracked lips during the winter or in hot, dry climates. Think about popping a small humidifier in your workspace or wherever you spend the most time.

It might seem like a quick fix to lick your lips to keep them moist, but that can make things worse. Saliva evaporates quickly, leaving a sticky residue that can attract bacteria and lead to infection. So, keep your tongue away from your lips and remember this: “Licking your lips will cause them to lickety-split.”

Whether from frigid cold or dry heat, your skin can lose water rapidly, causing cracking, flaking, discoloration, or swelling. So avoid jumping from a sweltering afternoon at the beach into a freezing cold movie theater.

Also, skip the hot showers or cold plunges for a bit. These types of rapid temperature changes will quickly dry out your lip corners. Bonus tip: Your lips can take a beating from the sun, so find a lip balm with SPF protection.

If your cracked lip corners don’t improve or become especially painful or swollen in a few days, it’s time to visit a board-certified dermatologist. If left untreated, angular cheilitis can last for years, leaving your lips discolored or scarred.

FYI: Angular cheilitis might not appear as clearly in people with darker skin. Instead of turning red, the affected skin may look pale and have a darker border.

Remember that lickety-split mantra? It’s for real. Saliva can get deposited in the corners of your lips for many reasons, like drooling, smoking, or sleeping with your mouth open due to some sniffles. Bacteria grows in those little saliva pools, triggering an inflammatory response that causes your lip corners to get irritated and crack.

Following these tips will make your lips feel better in about a week. Really bad cases of angular cheilitis can take a few weeks. Avoid smoking and eat a balanced diet to get faster results.

As mentioned above, Vaseline and other occlusives help create a protective barrier over the cracked lip corners, which helps the healing process.

You might have woken up with cracked lip corners, but you won’t be able to get rid of them overnight. Be patient and follow the tips above!

Talk to a dermatologist for customized care if your lip corners become red, swollen, or more painful after a few days.

#9064. Solid cork forms walls of pavilion dedicated to silence at Casa No Tempo in Alentejo

Photography by Mercês Tomaz Gomes

Antwerp-based studio Corkinho has unveiled its latest “still room”, a pavilion with walls of solid cork, which is installed in the grounds of a vacation villa designed by Manuel Aires Mateus.

The still room is a space dedicated to silent and introspective activities, such as reading, yoga, tea ceremonies or meditation.

Corkinho installed it in the grounds of Casa No Tempo, a former farmhouse in southern Portugal, which architect Aires Mateus converted into a holiday home in 2014 for hospitality entrepreneur João Rodrigues.

Lead designer Cédric Etienne devised the building’s innovative structure, which is fully demountable, with the help of architect and master carpenter Gonçalo Madeira Marrote of Madeiguincho.

The floor slab is a timber deck, built over a foundation of removable concrete blocks.

Above this, solid blocks of cork are stacked up like giant bricks to form the building’s walls and secured with metal rods that thread through milled channels.

The pavilion is topped by a timber roof, described by Etienne as “like a hat with four screws”, which helps to weigh down the cork blocks.

“I wanted it to be zero waste and carbon-neutral,” the designer told Dezeen.

“If we need to dismantle it, we can place it somewhere else. There is no glue and no screws,” he said.

“It’s like the Japanese way of building teahouses, with total respect of the local materials and no harm to the land.”

As the name suggests, Corkinho is a studio that specialises in objects and spaces built from cork.

The studio first launched the still room concept in 2020, when it moved its office into the former Noorderpershuis power station in Antwerp and transformed one of the rooms into a silent sanctuary.

Etienne defines a still room as any space where you can pause your mind and be still.

“It’s a place where you disconnect from noise and distractions and invite a deeper sense of presence,” he said.

After consulting with various hotel brands keen to adopt the concept, Etienne pitched the idea to Rodrigues and his company, Silent Living.

The company has five properties, all designed by Aires Mateus and all with a focus on slow living.

“I had been to Casa No Tempo many times, so I knew the place like an inner home,” the designer said.

“It felt so aligned in terms of feeling and senses, so I thought it could be a really beautiful challenge to move the concept forward in this place,” he continued.

The room can be used by guests staying at the villa, but it can also accommodate curated programmes.

Etienne has been hosting four-day silent retreats, allowing groups of designers and hospitality professionals to learn more about the still room concept.

The cork blocks, supplied by locally based company Sofalca, were heat-treated to improve their durability. The material gives the building impressive sensorial and thermal qualities, Etienne said.

“All the technical properties of cork – the acoustics, the scent, the softness – all become architectural conditions,” he stated.

“You really feel like you’re coming into a womb. Even when it’s 40 degrees outside, the temperature inside is around 22 or 23.”

Other pavilions recently featured in Dezeen include a wildlife pavilion informed by rippling water and a jigsaw-like pavilion made of mass-timber scrap.

Photography by Mercês Tomaz Gomes

#9061. Yes, Your Feet Age. Dermal Fillers Can Help

Barefoot walks on the beach. A day in their favorite high heels. A long training walk ahead of the Camano de Santiago. These are the goals—big and small—of women undergoing foot filler treatments.

Using an injectable filler—such as hyaluronic acid or body fat—to add padding to sore feet is not new, though it is gaining in popularity. As early as the 1960s, medical-grade silicone has been used to puff up padding deflated by age, years of wear and tear, and fashionable footwear, especially high heels. All of this puts intense pressure on the balls of the feet—otherwise known as the metatarsals.

Over time, the fatty cushion on the bottom of your feet dissipates. Fat pad atrophy affects 30% of people over the age of 60. Without that natural cushion, the bones in your feet come into closer contact with the ground, which causes a deep bruise-like pain in the heels or balls of the feet when walking barefoot or standing for long periods.

For some perspective, look at the doughy wonders that are baby feet and compare them to yours. As we age, wear and tear breaks down that plush tissue. And if you put your feet to heavy use, you’ll wear down that cushion quicker. Some of that internal cushioning can be restored—even if just temporarily—with the injection of dermal fillers.

“It’s getting very popular because people are already familiar with it for aesthetic [uses],” says Ben Pearl, DPM, a podiatrist at Arlington Foot and Ankle in Arlington, Virginia. Dr. Pearl specializes in sports medicine and treats endurance athletes looking to restore cushion lost in their feet from pounding the pavement.

Patients don’t have just one choice for injectables, though. Many of the same options available for cosmetic use have also shown promise for feet. There’s hyaluronic acid filler, which adds physical volume and cushioning, and calcium hydroxylapatite, such as Radiesse, which adds firm volume while also promoting new collagen growth. Sometimes human body fat is used as the injectable, known as adipose tissue, a practice that is quickly becoming the preferred method.

“[A fat injection] actually recruits your body to rebuild the fat pad in that area so it has a much longer duration,” says Anne Sharkey, DPM, of Soley Podiatry in Austin. Fat allografts from brands like Liposana and Leneva may last as long as two years, compared to hyaluronic acid fillers, which typically need a touch up in six to nine months.

This type of regenerative medicine is appealing to patients. It’s not a promise that the foot will return to its former glory, but that it will be “as close to normal as possible,” says Dr. Pearl.

Dr. Sharkey and Dr. Pearl have both seen positive results from their patients. Scientific studies corroborate the efficacy of the treatment as well. One small study looking at patients with metatarsal pain found five patients had no more pain six months post-hyaluronic acid injections, and those who still had pain could wear high heels twice as long as they could before the injections. Another study surveying patients who had been injected with body fat reported that their pain improved by more than 70 percent on average, 20 months post injection.

While there are a growing number of cosmetic clinics offering the procedure, Dr. Pearl cautions against allowing just any injector at it. That’s because injecting filler into feet is a more complex procedure than an aesthetic injection. For one, knowing where to inject requires an understanding of the foot’s pressure points. In his own practice, Dr. Pearl uses ultrasound to help determine where to replace the fat to offload the pain. Additionally, Dr. Pearl notes, the skin is much tougher on the feet than the face, making it a more complicated area to inject.

This is one reason why Dr. Sharkey set up her practice to include a nail salon—combining cosmetology and podiatry. Her patients are already familiar with dermal fillers. Within the attached nail salon you can get manicures, pedicures, ingrown nail treatment, toenail reconstruction, or dermal fillers for feet.

Try not to groan, but it depends. The cost of the procedure is influenced by how much filler is injected, and which brand is used. Other factors that affect cost include how your provider bills the procedure, and how much experience they have with dermal filler injections.

For cosmetic use, the American Society of Plastic Surgeons places the average cost of hyaluronic acid filler treatment at $715. They estimate nonhyaluronic acid fillers, including Radiesse, Sculptra, and Liposana to cost $901 on average per treatment. However, the feet will almost certainly require more filler than the face, so you can expect the cost to be higher.

But will insurance cover it? Unlikely. “Even though it isn't technically cosmetic, it may not be considered medically necessary, because these procedures are often considered elective and cosmetic branding has a box drawn around it,” says Mark Welter, chief strategy and growth officer at Welter Healthcare Partners, a healthcare business management firm.

If you’re transparent with your provider about any financial concerns you have, they can work with you to find a middle ground between pain relief and high costs. Dr. Sharkey, for example, will often offer her patients more affordable hyaluronic acid fillers as temporary pain relief until they’re ready to dive into a more expensive fat injection.

If injectables aren’t accessible to you, there are other ways to deal with foot pain. Here are some options, most of which require a low financial investment.

A podiatrist can help walk you through any of these options and come up with a plan to minimize your pain.

#9060. Many London architecture firms not paying London Living Wage

The majority of the London-based studios in The Pay 100‘s fifth annual salary survey are not paying Part I architectural assistants the London Living Wage, as required by the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA).

An engineering firm has topped the leaderboard for the average salaries for UK architects, according to a survey conducted by the anonymous group The Pay 100.

Engineering firm tops architect salary leaderboard

Published over the weekend, the survey provides rough figures only based on the mean figures submitted by respondents. This year’s data collected the annual salary of 127 firms in the UK and the mean number of hours of unpaid overtime per week.

Topping the leaderboard with the highest average annual salary for architects with less than five years’ experience is BakerHicks, an engineering and design firm, which paid £72,000.

Second on the list is London studio Hopkins Architects at £63,700, and joint third at £56,300 are London practices Samuel Chisholm Studio and Thomas Alexander Design.

The survey also presented figures for Part I and Part II architectural assistants. Transport for London had the highest wage for Part II roles at £44,000, followed by Foster + Partners at £42,000.

Majority of London firms not paying London Living Wage

The results for Part I roles included salaries from 30 studios, 21 of which were based in Greater London.

Only the top four studios on the leaderboard – Haworth Tompkins, Allford Hall Monaghan Morris, Studio McW and Studio PDP – paid more than the London Living Wage of £32,136, which RIBA declared a requirement for relevant offices.

Twelve of the 30 studios were paying Part I roles less than the £29,328 UK Living Wage.

Low wages “a threat to the future of the profession”

Alongside its survey data, The Pay 100 wrote an open letter to RIBA, asking it to take action on the financial wellbeing of those working in the architecture industry and to ensure the long-term future of the profession.

“Our aim has always been to create tangible financial incentives for employers to improve pay, empower employees to make informed career decisions, and encourage a healthier, more sustainable profession,” said The Pay 100 in the letter.

“We recognise that architecture practices operate within a highly competitive market, often under significant financial pressure themselves,” it continued. “Nevertheless, the commercial challenges facing practices should not prevent the profession from addressing the deteriorating conditions experienced by many employees.”

“Poor financial conditions for staff are not merely an employment issue; they are a threat to the long-term health, resilience and future of the profession.”

It went on to set out two courses of action it called for RIBA to take: establishing “meaningful minimum salaries” for RIBA chartered practices, and taking full ownership of The Pay 100 and its annual salary survey.

The Pay 100 said a framework of minimum salary levels should be established across different architecture roles, increasing year-on-year in line with inflation.

“A profession cannot sustainably advocate for the value of its services while leaving the financial conditions of its workforce to market pressures alone,” it said. “The RIBA should take a leading role in addressing this imbalance.”

After five years of aiming to improve pay transparency with its annual surveys, The Pay 100 wants RIBA to take ownership of the survey and commit resources to it, developing it into an industry-wide initiative.

“We believe that improving pay transparency across UK architecture should be a core responsibility of the profession’s leading membership body,” said The Pay 100.

“Under the RIBA’s stewardship, the survey could benefit from significantly greater reach, sustained institutional support and broader participation across the profession,” it continued.

“This would provide a foundation for more comprehensive salary data, stronger engagement between employers and employees, and meaningful progress towards better financial conditions throughout the industry.”

The Pay 100 ended its letter by asking for a public response from RIBA by 1 December

#9059. What Does Dark Green Poop Mean? Causes, Diet, and When to See a Doctor

Bum nuggets typically sport a classic brown, so glancing back into the loo and spying on greenish-colored poop can throw you for a loop.

Most of the time, green poop reflects a leafy diet or your body’s unique way of breaking things down. But if the green becomes a recurring (fecal) matter, it might be something else.

Continue reading to learn more about poop color, its meaning, and when it’s time to make an appointment with a healthcare provider.

Spotting green or another unexpected color in the toilet can be startling, but it’s more common than you might think. From dietary influences to your body’s digestion speed, several factors can change poop from earthy tones to other shades. Let’s check some out.

Are you chowing down on lots of green leafy veggies like spinach, kale, or broccoli? These foods are high in chlorophyll, which can dye your doodles green. Chlorophyll doesn’t always break down entirely before reaching your intestines, meaning it passes through your system and colors your stool green.

Have you ever had a St. Paddy’s Day-themed milkshake or a brightly colored cake? Artificial colors in foods and drinks can change poop from brown to green. It’s not magic! It’s just the dye in green food passing through your gut unchanged.

When your digestive system processes food too rapidly, it doesn’t allow for the full breakdown of bile, a yellow-green fluid that aids digestion. This often results in a greenish stool, especially during fast-moving episodes of diarrhea.

Have you recently been taking antibiotics? These meds can reset your gut’s bacterial crew. Since these tiny critters play a big part in the shade of your stool, introducing antibiotics might cause green poop sometimes.

If you’ve had certain medical treatments, it can affect digestion and cause bright green poop. One example is graft-versus-host disease, which may occur with bone marrow transplants. This tricky condition can bring about less-than-welcome guests, like diarrhea and green stool. It’s a clear signal from your body that things are out of sync.

Some uninvited microscopic guests like Salmonella bacteria, the water-loving mini parasite Giardia, and norovirus can also be a reason for your poop turning green. These critters can hustle your digestion at an unnaturally quick pace, turning your stool green as they disrupt your gut’s usual rhythm.

Babies can surprise you with a whole crayon box of poop colors, and green is definitely in the mix.

For infants, green stool might stem from the same factors as adults, like dietary changes. This includes adjustments when they start eating solids or changes in a parent’s diet if chestfeeding.

Another harmless cause could be ingesting a small amount of amniotic fluid in the womb. So, if you notice your little one sporting some spring grass-colored diapers, it’s usually no biggie.

If the green theme park in your toilet isn’t closing down, or if it’s accompanied by other symptoms like severe stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhea, it might be time to call in the pros. Persistent changes in stool color may signal underlying health issues that need medical attention.

Dark green poop can result from eating lots of leafy greens or foods with green coloring. However, it can also indicate that food travels quickly through the digestive system.

While liver issues can change stool color, they usually turn it pale or dark, not green. If you’re worried about liver health, look for pale or clay-colored stools instead.

If you haven’t been on a kale-eating spree, dark green poop might be from iron supplements or constipation remedies, which can also give poop a greenish tint.

Dark poop could be a sign of your diet or medications. However, if it’s black and tar-like, it might mean bleeding in your upper gastrointestinal tract. In that case, chatting with a healthcare professional is a must.

While green poop can def throw you through a loop, it’s usually not a sign of anything serious. It’s often your body’s way of dealing with what you eat or how fast you digest. So, unless it’s paired with other worrying symptoms, there’s probably no need to panic.

#9058. In the Wake of the 2024 Floods in Southern Brazil: Restore the Past or Rethink the Future?

In May 2024, the floods that hit Rio Grande do Sul exposed a contradiction common to contemporary cities. Many were built alongside rivers and shaped by their presence, yet spent decades trying to control water without incorporating its dynamics into urban planning. Extreme weather events will intensify that vulnerability. More than two years later, reconstruction in the Brazilian state has progressed, infrastructure has been restored, and new protection strategies are taking shape. But are these cities rebuilding their relationship with water, or only restoring the systems that failed?

Porto Alegre: Strengthening Defenses, Rethinking Resilience

In Porto Alegre, the state capital, home to approximately 1.4 million inhabitants, the response has focused in part on restoring and modernizing the flood protection system designed in the 1960s. The system comprises approximately 68 kilometers of levees, 14 passages originally equipped with floodgates, and 23 stormwater pumping stations. In May 2024, the Guaíba River reached 5.37 meters, well above the three-meter flood level. The scale of the event exposed weaknesses in both the physical barriers and the operation and integration of different components of the urban infrastructure, laying bare the lack of maintenance of these structures.

However, progress in structural interventions does not reduce the amount of work that remains. The city government plans to expand urban drainage with 9 new pumping stations, 26 kilometers of drainage networks and galleries, 11 stormwater detention basins, and 2 kilometers of linear park. The improvements, distributed across different watersheds, are expected to be completed by 2031.

However, progress in structural interventions does not reduce the amount of work that remains. A key limitation of a strategy based primarily on levees, walls, and pumps is that these structures cannot eliminate risk under all circumstances. These structures are essential in densely populated areas, but when water exceeds their design capacity, or they fail, the city can be suddenly exposed. In addition, barriers that protect certain areas can hinder rainwater drainage within those zones. Resilience therefore depends on combining conventional infrastructure with solutions that slow runoff, increase water storage capacity, and restore space to waterways.

This is precisely where the sponge city approach, developed and promoted in several Chinese cities, offers a complementary perspective. Rather than relying exclusively on pipes and channels to carry water away as quickly as possible, the strategy seeks to absorb and gradually release rainwater. The Chinese experience is particularly interesting because it demonstrates that this transformation need not be limited to small or sparsely developed cities. The sponge city approach can also be incorporated into major urban centers by retrofitting existing squares, streets, parking lots, schoolyards, and public spaces.

Indeed, the approach is widely advocated by urban planning scholars in Porto Alegre, considering the city particularly well suited to implementing this strategy. This perspective does not imply replicating the Chinese model wholesale, but rather adapting its underlying principles to Porto Alegre's existing natural features, including its waterways and remaining green areas.

Despite these favorable conditions, some ongoing urban interventions appear to be moving in the opposite direction. For example, repaving large areas of the city center with concrete pavers raises questions about how much permeability and water absorption are being incorporated into the city's reconstruction efforts. Rather than moving toward a sponge city, Porto Alegre risks becoming a paver city.

Cruzeiro do Sul: Rebuilding on Safer Ground

If Porto Alegre represents the challenge of transforming an established metropolis, Cruzeiro do Sul offers a more radical example of territorial reconstruction. Located in the Taquari Valley, approximately 126 kilometers from Porto Alegre, the municipality has 11,600 inhabitants. In 2024, flooding along the Taquari River severely affected the city, forcing approximately half the population to leave their homes and affecting around 95% of commercial establishments.

If Porto Alegre represents the challenge of transforming an established metropolis, Cruzeiro do Sul offers a more radical example of territorial reconstruction. Located in the Taquari Valley, approximately 126 kilometers from Porto Alegre, the municipality has 11,600 inhabitants. In 2024, flooding along the Taquari River severely affected the city, forcing approximately half the population to leave their homes and affecting around 95% of commercial establishments.

In the Passo de Estrela neighborhood, for example, more than 600 houses were destroyed. However, rather than rebuilding the community on the same site, the adopted strategy calls for relocating it to higher ground, approximately three kilometers from the former neighborhood. The project includes 150 houses, 174 plots, recreational areas, environmental preservation areas, and plots designated for public facilities such as a school and a church. The plan also includes commercial areas and public gathering spaces. Construction began in May 2026, and the schedule anticipates delivering homes between December 2026 and October 2027. On the original site, the proposal is to establish a memorial park and prohibit new residential construction.

The difference from Porto Alegre is significant. While the capital seeks to strengthen and complement its protection infrastructure, Cruzeiro do Sul may need to reorganize an affected territory completely. In smaller areas, where development is less dense and land is relatively more available, relocation may be more feasible. Even so, resettlement is not a simple solution. The success of relocation depends not only on providing safer homes, but also on enabling residents to maintain the relationships and support networks built in their former neighborhood.

Homes Delivered, a City Still to Be Built

Beyond the cities mentioned, numerous other municipalities are undergoing reconstruction. Returning to the housing figures, in February 2026, the federal government reported that more than 10,000 homes had been contracted through the "assisted purchase" program, which allows eligible families to choose new or existing properties in areas considered safe. In April 2026, the federal government's reconstruction report indicated that 12,468 housing units had been delivered through this program, with approximately 25,000 homes contracted or in the process of being contracted across all housing initiatives.

In April 2026, the federal government's reconstruction report indicated that 12,468 housing units had been delivered through this program, with approximately 25,000 homes contracted or in the process of being contracted across all housing initiatives.

Although significant, these figures require careful interpretation. Contracted homes are not necessarily delivered homes, and handing over a house does not, in itself, mean that a family has recovered its previous living conditions. Purchasing an existing property can speed up assistance, but it can also relocate families far from their former places of work, study, and social interaction. The challenge is to prevent the housing response from creating new problems of segregation.

Rebuilding Also Means Deciding Where Not to Build

Two years later, Rio Grande do Sul has seen tangible changes, but the reconstruction also reveals the gap between restoring infrastructure and transforming urbanization. The next step is to translate climate adaptation into master plans, building codes, and housing policies that recognize the limits of land occupation. This means preventing new construction in areas where risk cannot be mitigated, restoring floodplains and wetlands, increasing soil permeability, and combining protection systems with nature-based solutions.

The heavy rains of June 2025 offered a further reminder of the state's vulnerability. More than 120 municipalities were affected by flooding and landslides after intense rainfall caused rivers to overflow, particularly in the central and western regions of Rio Grande do Sul.

These events do not, by themselves, prove that reconstruction efforts have failed, as major infrastructure projects take years to complete and different rainfall events produce different impacts. However, they reinforce the need to rethink what reconstruction should achieve. The question that should guide the coming years is not how to restore cities to the way they looked before May 2024, but how to build cities better than those that existed before the floods. Cities in which water is neither ignored nor treated as an enemy, but recognized as a natural force that must be part of urban design.
